title: Breakdowns & Warning Triangles
whatItIs: If you break down, think first about other road users. Get off the road if you can and warn traffic.
keyFacts: Put a warning triangle at least 45 metres behind your car, on the same side of the road.
Never use a warning triangle on a motorway.
Don't stand between your car and oncoming traffic.
Wear light-coloured or fluorescent clothing in daylight, and reflective clothing at night or in poor visibility.
Keep your sidelights on if it is dark or visibility is poor.

visual.caption: If you break down on an ordinary road

items.title: Get off the road
items.text: Get your vehicle off the road if possible, ideally a place designed for parking or a lay-by.

items.title: Hazard lights on
items.text: If your car is blocking traffic. Sidelights too after dark.

items.title: Stand clear
items.text: Don't stand between your car and oncoming traffic, or where you hide its lights at night.

items.title: Triangle 45 m back
items.text: On the same side of the road. Never on a motorway.

items.title: Call for help
items.text: Stay off the road and well away from your car while you wait.

onTheTest.question: How far behind your broken-down car should you put a warning triangle on an ordinary road?
onTheTest.why: Place it at least 45 metres behind, on the same side of the road. Never use one on a motorway.

traps: At night or in poor visibility, don't stand where you hide your lights from drivers behind.
45 m, on the same side of the road as your car.
